# User block list

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:user-block-list` · **Epic:** [#46](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/46) · **Tickets:** 12 (10S 2M)

Admins can block a person by Dex sub or email from the console. The list is stored on the CP outside policy versions, ships to workers on the policy wire as `blockedUsers`, and workers deny any request or session whose identity claims match, within one long-poll cycle. This is the P1 offboarding and incident kill switch. In P1 attribute mode a request that carries no token at all is not matched; P2 require mode closes that gap.

## How we build it

- CP store: cpstate table `blocked_users(id, sub, email, reason, created_by, created_at)`. Each row needs sub or email; email is trimmed and lowercased on write; unique indexes on sub and email. The table is outside policy_versions, so a rollback can never unblock anyone. The list is capped at `config.MaxBlockedUsers` (5000) entries and at `config.MaxBlockedUsersBytes` (512 KiB) of serialized JSON, whichever is hit first.
- Go API `controlplane.BlockStore{List, Add(ctx, entry, actor), Remove(ctx, id, actor)}` is shared by the HTTP handlers and by P3 offboarding, which calls `BlockStore.Add` with actor `system:offboarding` instead of writing a policy version. Every mutation runs the shared validator and calls `policyServer.Refresh()`; the HTTP path (W-P1-BLOCK-11) additionally goes through the admin audit `StateHasher` for target `blocked_users`, and offline CLI writes are audited through `adminaudit.OpenForCLI`.
- Wire: new `config.BlockedUser{Sub, Email}` (json `sub,omitempty` / `email,omitempty`) and `config.Policy.BlockedUsers` (json `blockedUsers,omitempty`, yaml `policy.blockedUsers`). `remoteWire` embeds `Policy`, so workers decode it with no extra code. `policyWire.BlockedUsers` is added with omitempty and holds only sub and email (reason and actor stay on the CP). Entries are deduplicated and sorted by (sub, email), so an empty list keeps /policy byte-identical and the ETag only changes on a real change. `Policy.DeepCopy` copies the slice.
- Validation: one exported `config.ValidateBlockedUsers` runs in YAML parse, in `parseRemotePolicy`, and in the CP write path before insert. The CP can therefore never serve an entry that workers reject, which would otherwise make every worker keep its last-known-good policy and freeze all policy updates.
- CP load: a `blocked_users` serve-time overlay registered through the policy server's overlay seam (W-P1-PVER-11) adds the `BlockStore` list to the wire `policyServer.loadPolicy` builds (from YAML today, from the head version after W-P1-PVER-01). A block-list read error makes `loadPolicy` fail, so `Refresh` keeps the last-known-good wire and ETag; the list is never served empty by accident. A `policy.blockedUsers` key in the CP policy file is ignored with a warning (console API only) and is preserved by `Server.WritePolicy`.
- Worker install: `policy.Evaluator.load` builds a sub set and a lowercase email set from `p.BlockedUsers`, so `Replace` swaps them under the same `swapMu` as allow/deny. This covers boot (`policy.NewEvaluator` in worker.go), `longPollControlPlane` (`ev.Replace`) and standalone YAML with no extra wiring. New method `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` is added to `policy.Evaluator` and to `proxy.PolicyEvaluator`. Until the first pull the worker stays fail-closed as today.
- Worker match (deny-only, fail closed): the check uses the claims of any token the worker parsed in W-P1-VRFY-02 (W-P1-BLOCK-02), whatever its verification status (valid, expired, bad signature), because a match can only deny. Sub is an exact match and email a lowercase match. Raw tokens are never logged. Cost per check: one read lock and at most two map lookups.
- Enforcement points: at CONNECT after Proxy-Authorization identity extraction and before any dial or `200 Connection Established` (covers raw tunnels too); in a new `blockStage` of `runRequestStages` after the identity stage and before `constraintGate` (the first policy gate); `runRequestStages` is the one pipeline for HTTP/1 requests, h2 and gRPC streams (#388) and WebSocket upgrade requests, so no separate per-stream check exists.
- Live termination: `internal/proxy` keeps a registry of open sessions keyed by normalized sub and email (raw tunnels, HTTP/1 keep-alive, HTTP/2 connections and WebSocket frame pumps). After a policy change is applied, the worker closes the sessions that now match the list and writes one deny event per closed session, so idle and long-lived sessions are cut (not drained) at apply time. A request that arrived before the block completes; the connection is then closed. Propagation: about 1 s after `BlockStore.Add` (it wakes held long-polls), plus at most 2 s for offline CLI writes, and at most the 15 s backoff plus one round trip for a worker recovering from CP errors (W-P1-BLOCK-05).
- Deny response: `403` with JSON `{"error":"user_blocked"}` on the CONNECT response, the request or the h2 stream, then the session ends. The event has Decision=deny, Reason=`user_blocked` and the user fields from W-P1-VRFY-03, and the worker calls `RecordBlocked("user_blocked")`. The alert bridge raises a high-severity Finding deduplicated per user (key derived from a hash of the sub); the Finding carries the opaque sub only, never the email.
- Console coupling: the API refuses a request from an admin to remove a block that matches their own identity (another admin or break-glass must do it). The CP session layer rejects login and active sessions for a principal whose sub or email is blocked.
- Rollout safety: workers advertise `caps:["blocklist/v1"]` on heartbeat (W-P1-BLOCK-10). Old workers decode the new wire without error (encoding/json drops unknown fields) and would otherwise look current. The CP registry stores the caps and the Blocked users panel (W-P1-BLOCK-04) and worker list warn about connected workers that do not enforce the list.
- Degraded modes: while the CP is unreachable, workers keep their last-known-good list and never unblock on their own; new blocks apply when they reconnect. If Dex is down, admins use break-glass (W-P1-OPS1-08). A CP without --state-dir has no store: the block-list API returns 503 `state_dir_required` and /policy is unchanged. Operators can also block and unblock offline with `warden control-plane block add|remove|list --state-dir` (W-P1-BLOCK-08), which a running CP picks up within 2s.
- Standalone (local-only) workers accept `policy.blockedUsers` in local YAML, with the same validation and enforcement. It applies on restart, since there is no local hot-reload today.
- Known P1 gap: a blocked user whose agent sends no token at all is treated as anonymous in attribute mode and is not matched. P2 require mode (identity-enforcement) closes this. Transparent mode (`proxy.mode: transparent`) has no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization, so only requests carrying an `X-Warden-Identity` header are matched there; this is the same gap. Every `Evaluator.Replace` also resets rate-limit windows, so each block or unblock resets them fleet-wide; this is documented and left to a follow-up.

## Done when

On a managed deployment where every connected worker advertises blocklist/v1, an admin blocks alice@corp in the console (or with break-glass when Dex is down), and the block is audited. Within one long-poll cycle Alice's new CONNECTs get 403 user_blocked whether her token is valid or expired; her open HTTP/1 keep-alive, HTTP/2, WebSocket and tunnel sessions are closed or denied with deny events carrying reason user_blocked and her sub; one Finding is raised for her; other users are unaffected; and she can no longer use the console. A CP block-list read error, a policy rollback, a worker restart and a CP outage each leave her blocked. Unblocking restores access and returns the served ETag to its previous value. Requests with no token at all are a documented P1 gap closed by P2 require mode.

### 1/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-01

**Carry blockedUsers in config.Policy and the policy wire**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#47](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/47)

**Context.** The User block list lets an admin block a person by Dex sub or email; the list ships to workers on the policy wire as `blockedUsers`, and workers deny any request or session whose identity claims match. This ticket is the wire foundation only: the `config.BlockedUser` type, `Policy.BlockedUsers`, one shared normalizer and validator, and `policyWire.BlockedUsers`. With no entries nothing changes: `/policy` stays byte-identical and the ETag is the same. The shared validator is what lets the CP refuse any entry a worker would reject, so a bad row can never freeze policy updates across the fleet. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** enforcement on the worker (W-P1-BLOCK-02), the CP store that fills the list (W-P1-BLOCK-03), and everything user-facing.

**What to build.** Types, YAML/JSON plumbing, `normalizeBlockedUsers` and `ValidateBlockedUsers` with a count limit and a total serialized-size limit.

**Requirements**

- New `config.BlockedUser{Sub, Email}` with yaml `sub`/`email` and json `sub,omitempty`/`email,omitempty`; new `Policy.BlockedUsers []BlockedUser` with json `blockedUsers,omitempty`, and `blockedUsers` added to `rawConfig.Policy` so strict YAML decoding (`KnownFields(true)`) accepts it.
- New `normalizeBlockedUsers` runs in both `parse()` and `parseRemotePolicy`: trim spaces, lowercase email, dedupe, sort by (sub, email).
- New exported `config.ValidateBlockedUsers`, called from `validate()`: each entry needs sub or email, sub at most 255 bytes, email at most 254 bytes and containing '@', no control characters, at most `config.MaxBlockedUsers` (5000) entries, AND the JSON serialization of the whole list at most `config.MaxBlockedUsersBytes` (512 KiB, half of the worker's 1 MiB `maxPolicyBytes` in internal/config/remote.go). The size check is the real bound: 5000 entries of maximum length would be about 2.5 MB, so the original 'MaxBlockedUsers entries stay under 512 KiB' claim was impossible. Errors name the entry index or `total size`, never the value.
- `Policy.DeepCopy` copies `BlockedUsers` so `GetPolicy` callers never share the backing array.
- `controlplane.policyWire` (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) gains `BlockedUsers []config.BlockedUser` json `blockedUsers,omitempty` (sub and email only; reason and actor stay on the CP). `policyServer.loadPolicy` does NOT copy a YAML list into it and logs a warning when the CP policy file contains one (the console API is the only source; W-P1-BLOCK-03 merges the stored list).
- `controlplane.policyYAML` gains `BlockedUsers` so `Server.WritePolicy` never drops the key from the file.
- Default off: an absent or empty list changes no behaviour and adds no log lines.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first (they fail to compile until the type exists): internal/config (config_test.go, remote_test.go) and internal/controlplane (controlplane_test.go).
2. internal/config/config.go: add type BlockedUser, consts MaxBlockedUsers and MaxBlockedUsersBytes, field Policy.BlockedUsers, the rawConfig.Policy key, the slice copy in Policy.DeepCopy.
3. internal/config/config.go: add normalizeBlockedUsers and the exported ValidateBlockedUsers; call the normalizer in parse() and the validator from validate().
4. internal/config/remote.go: call normalizeBlockedUsers in parseRemotePolicy before validate; remoteWire already decodes the field through the embedded Policy.
5. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add BlockedUsers to policyWire (omitempty) and to policyYAML; internal/controlplane/policyserver.go loadPolicy: warn when p.BlockedUsers is non-empty and do not serve it.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With no blocked users, GET /policy body and ETag are byte-identical to a golden captured before the change: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWireBlockedUsersOmittedWhenEmpty`.
- [ ] A CP response with blockedUsers [{"sub":"u1"},{"email":"Alice@Corp.com "}] decodes to [{Email:"alice@corp.com"},{Sub:"u1"}]: `go test ./internal/config -run TestRemoteProvider_DecodesBlockedUsers`.
- [ ] An entry with neither field, or more than MaxBlockedUsers entries, fails parse from YAML and from remote JSON with an error naming the index, and RemoteProvider keeps its last-known-good policy: `go test ./internal/config -run TestBlockedUsersValidation`.
- [ ] 5000 short entries (sub of 20 bytes) validate and marshal under 512 KiB; a list of 1000 entries of maximum length (sub 255, email 254) exceeds MaxBlockedUsersBytes and is rejected with an error naming `total size` and not containing any entry value: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestBlockedUsersSizeLimit|TestBlockedUsersCountLimit'`.
- [ ] Mutating the slice returned by GetPolicy does not affect a second GetPolicy call: `go test -race ./internal/config -run TestPolicyDeepCopyBlockedUsers`.
- [ ] A dashboard policy edit through `Server.WritePolicy` keeps `policy.blockedUsers` in the file, and a CP policy file that contains the key logs the warning and serves no blockedUsers: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWritePolicyKeepsBlockedUsers|TestLoadPolicyIgnoresYAMLBlockedUsers'`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 2/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-02

**Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT and per request**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#48](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/48)

**Context.** Once the block list arrives on the policy wire (W-P1-BLOCK-01), the worker must deny every request from a blocked user. This ticket builds the block set inside `policy.Evaluator` so it is swapped atomically with allow/deny at boot, on every long-poll update and for standalone YAML, and checks it at CONNECT and in a new request stage. A match returns 403 `user_blocked`, records a deny event and ends the session. Matching uses the claims of any token the worker parsed, verified or not, because a match can only deny. It was narrowed in the 2026-10-19 split pass: advertising `blocklist/v1` in the heartbeat moved to W-P1-BLOCK-10; closing already-open sessions is W-P1-BLOCK-05. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** the heartbeat caps (W-P1-BLOCK-10), live termination of tunnels/keep-alives/h2/WebSocket (W-P1-BLOCK-05), the per-user Finding (W-P1-BLOCK-06) and the L1 harness scenarios (W-P1-BLOCK-09, which need the harness OIDC issuer from W-P1-VRFY-11). This ticket proves behaviour at package level with `fakes.Verifier` (W-P1-VRFY-01).

**Known gaps, documented:** a request that carries no token at all is anonymous in attribute mode and is not matched (P2 require mode closes it, W-P2-WBND-03). Transparent mode (`proxy.mode: transparent`, internal/proxy/transparent.go) has no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization, so the CONNECT check cannot run there; only requests that carry an `X-Warden-Identity` header on terminated traffic are matched by the per-request stage.

**What to build.** The block sets in `policy.Evaluator`, the declared deny reason, the CONNECT-time check, the `blockStage` and the JSON 403 response.

**Requirements**

- internal/policy/policy.go (existing `Evaluator`): `load` builds a `blockedSubs` set and a lowercase `blockedEmails` set from `p.BlockedUsers`; new `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` reads them under `swapMu.RLock`, so `Replace` swaps them atomically with allow/deny (boot via `policy.NewEvaluator`, `longPollControlPlane` via `ev.Replace`, standalone YAML with no extra wiring). Until the first pull the worker stays fail-closed as today. Every `Replace` also resets rate-limit windows, so each block or unblock resets them fleet-wide; this is documented and left to a follow-up.
- internal/proxy/proxy.go: add `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` to the `PolicyEvaluator` interface (currently EvaluateRequest and Replace); update the fake evaluators in internal/worker/loops_test.go, the proxy test fakes and test/fakes. `SettingsApplier` is not changed.
- internal/denyreason/reasons.go: add `UserBlocked Reason = "user_blocked"` to the declared set (the old plan's internal/proxy/reasons.go does not exist; JAUD-06 landed the contract). `TestNoReasonLiteralsOutsideTheDeclaredSet`, `TestDeclaredSetIsComplete` and the invariants suite keep passing; no `"user_blocked"` literal appears outside internal/denyreason.
- CONNECT check in `handleConn` (internal/proxy/serve.go:198): after the header loop and the identity extraction of W-P1-VRFY-02 (`connIdentity`) and BEFORE `EvaluateRequest`, any dial and the `200 Connection Established`; it covers both the TLS-terminating and the raw-tunnel path. On a match: record the deny through the deny chokepoint (`emitDenyEvent`/`storeDeny`, which W-P1-VRFY-03 routes through `recordEvent` so the user fields are stamped) with Protocol `tcp`, answer `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Length`, `Connection: close` and body `{"error":"user_blocked"}`, and close.
- Per-request check: a new `blockStage` in `runRequestStages` (internal/proxy/http.go:394), placed right after the identity stage of W-P1-VRFY-02 and before `constraintGate` (the first policy gate; `constraintGate` was added after the old plan and runs before `judgeGate`). `runRequestStages` is the ONE pipeline for HTTP/1 requests, h2 streams, gRPC streams (#388) and WebSocket upgrade requests (which pass the stages before the hijack), so this single stage covers all of them; the audit's per-stream check at the top of `serveGRPCStream` is not needed. On a match call `emitDeny(s, denyreason.UserBlocked, denyExtra{LatencyMs: s.latencyMs()})`, write the 403 JSON through a new `errorJSON(status int, body string)` method on `responseSink` (internal/proxy/sink.go, implemented by `connSink` and `h2Sink`; update test sinks) and end the session without forwarding, swapping secrets or calling the judge.
- Fail closed, deny-only: the claims of valid, expired and bad-signature tokens are all matched (W-P1-VRFY-01 returns the parsed sub and email for expired and invalid tokens and `connIdentity` keeps them for exactly this check). A sub is an exact match; an email is lowercased once when identity is resolved and matched against the lowercase set. Requests with no token are unaffected in attribute mode. The raw token is never logged; the event records `identity_status` so the cases can be told apart.
- The event has Decision=deny, Reason=`user_blocked` and the user fields of W-P1-VRFY-03; `emitDenyEvent` already calls `RecordRequest("deny", ...)` and `RecordBlocked("user_blocked")`.
- Hot path: `IsBlocked` takes one read lock and at most two map lookups and allocates nothing (asserted with `testing.AllocsPerRun`).
- Decision-log schema: `docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json` does not exist on main (W-P1-JAUD-02 creates it). If it has landed when this ticket merges, add `user_blocked` to its reason enum with a schema_rev bump here; otherwise W-P1-JAUD-02 takes the enum from `denyreason.Declared()`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/policy (IsBlocked, Replace swap, AllocsPerRun), internal/proxy (serve_test.go CONNECT deny with zero dials and raw-tunnel path, http_reuse_test.go kept-alive session denied on the next request after Replace, grpc_test.go and ws tests for the same stage, transparent-mode test), internal/worker (long-poll applies the list), internal/denyreason guard tests.
2. internal/policy/policy.go: blockedSubs/blockedEmails in load, IsBlocked. internal/proxy/proxy.go: extend PolicyEvaluator; update fakes.
3. internal/denyreason/reasons.go: add UserBlocked to the set and the declared list.
4. internal/proxy/serve.go: connect-time block check and 403 JSON before EvaluateRequest. internal/proxy/sink.go: add errorJSON to responseSink, connSink and h2Sink.
5. internal/proxy/http.go: new blockStage in runRequestStages after the identity stage and before constraintGate.
6. Add a short 'Enforcement' paragraph to docs/control-plane.md (the full Block list section is created by W-P1-BLOCK-05) stating the token-less and transparent-mode gaps.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A CONNECT whose Proxy-Authorization resolves to blocked sub u1 gets 403 {"error":"user_blocked"}, the fake dialer records zero dials, and one event has Reason=user_blocked and UserSub=u1: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestBlockList_ConnectDenied`.
- [ ] On a TLS keep-alive session for alice@corp.com that completed one allowed request, after `Replace` adds email ALICE@corp.com the next request gets 403 and the upstream sees exactly one request: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestBlockList_KeepAliveCut`.
- [ ] A request carrying an expired token and one carrying a bad-signature token for a blocked sub are denied; user u2 and a token-less request are forwarded unchanged: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestBlockList_ExpiredTokenDenied|TestBlockList_BadSignatureDenied|TestBlockList_OtherUsersUnaffected'`.
- [ ] A blocked user's gRPC stream and plain h2 stream on an existing h2 connection get 403 through the shared stage, and a WebSocket upgrade request from a blocked user gets 403 without the 101: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestBlockList_GRPCStreamDenied|TestBlockList_H2StreamDenied|TestBlockList_WebSocketUpgradeDenied'`.
- [ ] In transparent mode a request without identity is forwarded (documented gap) and one with a blocked `X-Warden-Identity` is denied: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestBlockList_TransparentMode`.
- [ ] A managed worker that long-polls a fake CP enforces blockedUsers right after `ev.Replace`: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestLongPollAppliesBlockList`.

- [ ] `IsBlocked` at 5000 entries allocates 0 per call: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestIsBlockedAllocs` (uses `testing.AllocsPerRun`); `go test -race ./internal/policy ./internal/proxy ./internal/worker` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 3/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-03

**Add the CP block-list store and merge it into the served policy**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#49](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/49)

**Context.** The block list lives on the control plane outside policy versions, so a rollback can never unblock anyone, and is merged into the served wire at serve time. This ticket adds the `blocked_users` cpstate table, the `BlockStore` Go API (the one write path, used by the admin API, the offline CLI and later by P3 offboarding with actor `system:offboarding`) and the `blocked_users` serve-time overlay. A store read error keeps the last-known-good policy instead of serving an empty list. It was split from the original W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49): the admin HTTP API is W-P1-BLOCK-11. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** HTTP routes, authz and audit rows (W-P1-BLOCK-11), console session revocation and the in-memory login snapshot (W-P1-BLOCK-07), the CLI and the `data_version` watcher (W-P1-BLOCK-08).

**What to build.** Migration, `BlockStore`, the overlay registered through W-P1-PVER-11, load-error handling with a Finding, and a constructor that works without a `Server` (for the CLI).

**Requirements**

- cpstate migration `blocklist/0001` (SSO-01 runner, ID convention `feature/NNNN`): `blocked_users(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sub TEXT, email TEXT, reason TEXT, created_by TEXT, created_at INTEGER)` with `CHECK(sub IS NOT NULL OR email IS NOT NULL)` and unique indexes on sub and email (stored trimmed/lowercase). Exported `controlplane.BlockMigrations()` for callers that open the DB themselves.
- New `controlplane.BlockStore` (internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go): `NewBlockStore(db *cpstate.DB, opts BlockStoreOptions{Clock, OnRefresh func()})` (no Server needed), `List(ctx)`, `Add(ctx, entry BlockEntry, actor string) (id string, err error)`, `Remove(ctx, id, actor string) error`, `Wire(ctx) ([]config.BlockedUser, error)` (normalized, sorted, sub/email only) and `OnChange(func())` (callbacks run after every successful in-process mutation; W-P1-BLOCK-07 and W-P1-BLOCK-08 register theirs). `Add` runs `config.ValidateBlockedUsers` on the resulting list (so count and total-size limits apply), reason is at most 512 bytes, id is `bu_` + 16 hex; errors `ErrInvalid`, `ErrDuplicate`, `ErrTooMany`, `ErrNotFound` map to 400/409/422/404 in W-P1-BLOCK-11. `created_by` records the actor string (`oidc:<sub>`, `cli:<user>`, `system:offboarding`). `BlockStore` is the only write path.
- Serve-time merge: register a `blocked_users` overlay (W-P1-PVER-11 `addOverlay`) in `controlplane.Run`/`New` only when `cfg.State != nil`; its `apply` sets `w.BlockedUsers` from `BlockStore.Wire` (helper `withBlockedUsers(wire)`) and returns a fingerprint (first 16 hex of sha256 of the canonical list, empty when the list is empty). Because it is an overlay the list is never part of a policy version, so a rollback or import cannot change it.
- Any store error fails `loadPolicy`, so `Refresh` keeps the previous wire and ETag (never an empty list by accident). The first failure of an episode logs one ERROR line `msg=blocklist_load_failed` (no entry values; repeats are suppressed until a load succeeds) and publishes a high-severity `blocklist_load_failed` Finding through `s.pipeline.CurrentManager().Bus().PublishFinding` (nil-guarded; the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1, so the log line is the signal when no pipeline exists).
- Each successful mutation calls `policyServer.Refresh()` (so held long-polls wake at once) and then the `OnChange` callbacks. A removal that restores the previous list returns the served ETag to its previous value.
- A CP without `--state-dir` (`cfg.State == nil`) builds no store, registers no overlay and serves a byte-identical `/policy`; the dashboard routes (W-P1-BLOCK-11) answer 503 `state_dir_required` there.
- Reason text and entry values are never written to slog or metrics by this ticket.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane (blockedusers_test.go), using an in-memory cpstate DB and a test policy server.
2. New internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go: migration, BlockStore, errors, the overlay helper withBlockedUsers and the load-failure handling.
3. internal/controlplane/run.go and controlplane.go: build the store when State != nil, register the overlay with the policy server, pass the pipeline for the Finding.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a worker long-poll waiting on the current ETag, `BlockStore.Add` of {email:"alice@corp.com"} makes the long-poll return 200 within 1s with blockedUsers [{"email":"alice@corp.com"}] and no reason field: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_AddWakesLongPoll`.
- [ ] After Add then Remove, GET /policy returns the original ETag and a byte-identical body; Remove of an unknown id returns ErrNotFound: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_RemoveRestoresETag`.
- [ ] A store read error during `Refresh` leaves the served ETag and blockedUsers unchanged, logs blocklist_load_failed once across repeated ticker refreshes and publishes one Finding: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_LoadErrorKeepsLastGood`.
- [ ] Add with neither field returns ErrInvalid, the same email in different case returns ErrDuplicate, the (MaxBlockedUsers+1)th entry returns ErrTooMany and a list over MaxBlockedUsersBytes is rejected: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_Validation`.
- [ ] A policy version created or rolled back (test policy store) leaves blockedUsers unchanged and `doc_json` never contains it: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_OutsidePolicyVersions`.
- [ ] A CP without State serves a /policy byte-identical to main, and the overlay is not registered: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_NoStateUnchanged`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 5/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-05

**Close open sessions of newly blocked users on policy change**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#240](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/240)

**Context.** Raw tunnels, idle HTTP/1 keep-alive connections, HTTP/2 connections and WebSocket frame pumps never pass through a per-request check, so a blocked user keeps them open indefinitely. This ticket adds a per-identity session registry in `internal/proxy` and closes the matching sessions after each applied policy change, making the epic's kill-switch claim hold for every connection type. It also creates the 'Block list' section of docs/control-plane.md. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** per-request denial (W-P1-BLOCK-02), the CP side and API (W-P1-BLOCK-03/11), and the agent-disabled closure of anonymous sessions (W-P2-AREG-05, which extends this registry).

**Semantics (decided here, from the review addendum of 2026-10-16).** A request that ARRIVED under the old policy completes under it. A SESSION (raw tunnel, keep-alive connection, h2 connection, WebSocket) matched by the new block list is CUT at apply time, not drained: the registry close interrupts active streams, not only new ones. Propagation bound: `BlockStore.Add` calls `Refresh`, which wakes held long-polls at once, so a connected worker applies the change within about 1 s; the offline CLI adds at most one 2 s `data_version` poll (W-P1-BLOCK-08); a worker backing off after control-plane errors applies it after at most the 15 s backoff plus one long-poll round trip (`controlPlane.longPollWait` defaults to 30 s and does not delay a changed policy). While the CP is unreachable a worker keeps its last list and never unblocks.

**What to build.** The registry, registration at the four session kinds, `Proxy.CloseBlockedSessions`, the worker hook and two metrics.

**Requirements**

- New internal/proxy/sessions.go: a registry mapping normalized sub and lowercase email to a set of `io.Closer` behind a mutex; sessions register when identity resolves (CONNECT, or the first request on a connection) and deregister on close. Sessions without identity are not registered (no overhead for anonymous traffic). Transparent-mode connections register only when an `X-Warden-Identity` header resolves.
- Register/deregister at: raw tunnels (`tunnel`, internal/proxy/serve.go:409), HTTP/1 keep-alive sessions (the session loop in internal/proxy/http.go), HTTP/2 connections from `handleGRPC` (internal/proxy/grpc.go:41) and WebSocket frame pumps after `s.handoff` (`handleWSUpgrade`, internal/proxy/ws.go:66).
- New method `Proxy.CloseBlockedSessions()` checks each registered identity with `IsBlocked` (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and closes matches; closing interrupts active streams. Each closed session writes exactly one deny event with Reason=`user_blocked` (through `emitDenyEvent`; Protocol per session kind) carrying the user's sub.
- Hook: `longPollControlPlane` (internal/worker/loops.go) already takes `onApply func()` and calls it after `ev.Replace(remote)`; `internal/worker/applier.go` already uses it (`applier.Apply` is passed at internal/worker/worker.go:935). Do NOT add a new parameter: compose with the existing callback (`func(){ applier.Apply(); p.CloseBlockedSessions() }`) so it runs for every applied change.
- Metrics (nil-safe methods on the proxy `MetricsRecorder` seam and `observability.Metrics`, plus `nopMetrics` and fakes): OTel gauge `warden.blocklist.entries` (Prometheus `warden_blocklist_entries`) set from the number of entries after each applied policy change, and counter `warden.blocklist.sessions_closed.total` (`warden_blocklist_sessions_closed_total`). No label carries identity.
- docs/control-plane.md: new 'Block list' section stating the semantics and the propagation bound above, the token-less (attribute mode) gap closed by P2 require mode, the transparent-mode limitation, and the degraded modes (CP unreachable keeps the last list; Dex down uses break-glass; no state dir means no store).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/proxy (sessions_test.go: tunnel, WebSocket, idle keep-alive, h2, mid-transfer, concurrent register and close under -race) and internal/worker (hook composition).
2. New internal/proxy/sessions.go: registry, register/deregister helpers, CloseBlockedSessions.
3. internal/proxy/serve.go tunnel, internal/proxy/http.go session loop, internal/proxy/grpc.go handleGRPC and internal/proxy/ws.go handleWSUpgrade: register and deregister the connection.
4. internal/worker/worker.go (where longPollControlPlane is started): compose the existing applier.Apply with proxy.CloseBlockedSessions.
5. internal/observability and internal/proxy (MetricsRecorder, nopMetrics, test fakes): add the two metrics.
6. docs/control-plane.md: add the Block list section.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An open raw tunnel and an open WebSocket session for a user are closed within 1s after the user is added and `CloseBlockedSessions` runs, with one user_blocked deny event each: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestBlockList_TunnelCut|TestBlockList_WebSocketCut'`.
- [ ] An idle HTTP/1 keep-alive connection and an h2 connection for a blocked user are closed without a further request: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestBlockList_IdleKeepAliveCut|TestBlockList_H2Cut'`.
- [ ] Race semantics: a CONNECT tunnel mid-transfer (slow fake upstream) dies within 1s of the block applying, while a request that arrived before the block completes normally and delivers its full response before its connection is closed: `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run 'TestBlockList_MidTransferTunnelCut|TestBlockList_InFlightRequestCompletes'`.
- [ ] Sessions of other users and anonymous sessions stay open; concurrent register and close is race-free; a long-poll update calls the composed hook and the settings applier still runs: `go test -race ./internal/proxy ./internal/worker -run 'TestBlockList_OtherSessionsStay|TestSessionRegistryRace|TestLongPollClosesBlockedSessions'`.
- [ ] `warden_blocklist_sessions_closed_total` increases by the number of closed sessions and `warden_blocklist_entries` reflects the list size (metrics fake): `go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/observability -run TestBlocklistMetrics`.
- [ ] docs/control-plane.md contains the 'Block list' section with the propagation bound and the stated gaps: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockListDocsMentionBounds`; `go test -race ./internal/proxy ./internal/worker` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#212--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT and per request

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-09`](user-block-list.md#912--w-p1-block-09) Add harness scenarios for blocking users and cutting their sessions; [`W-P2-AREG-05`](agent-registry.md#57--w-p2-areg-05) Bind workers to an agent id and enforce agent_disabled; [`W-P2-SECT-03`](security-tests.md#37--w-p2-sect-03) Add binding, cross-agent and issued-token lifetime cases; [`W-P2-WBND-09`](identity-enforcement.md#910--w-p2-wbnd-09) Close require-mode sessions at token expiry and document require mode

### 6/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-06

**Raise one user_blocked Finding per user without leaking email**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#241](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/241)

**Context.** Every blocked request is a `user_blocked` deny event. Today `bridgeEvent` (internal/alertpipeline/bridge.go) turns any event with a Reason into a Finding keyed on the domain, so one blocked user hitting many domains raises many alerts and none say who it was. This ticket gives `user_blocked` its own case with a per-user dedup key and high severity, and carries the opaque sub only, so no email reaches webhooks. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** raising the deny event (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and the pipeline's delivery rules.

**What to build.** `Subject.User`, a `user_blocked` branch in `bridgeEvent` and an entry in `reasonSeverity`.

**Requirements**

- internal/integration/types.go: add `User string` json `user,omitempty` to `integration.Subject`; it carries `UserSub` only, never email.
- `bridgeEvent` handles `Reason == string(denyreason.UserBlocked)` before the generic reason branch: DedupKey `user_blocked:` plus the first 16 hex chars of sha256(sub), Subject {Worker, User: sub} (Domain left empty so one user dedups across domains), Category security, Summary `user blocked: <hash8> denied` and Evidence `reason=user_blocked`, with no email, token or domain.
- `reasonSeverity` maps `user_blocked` to `SevHigh`. Other reasons keep their current DedupKey and severity.
- An event with Reason user_blocked but an empty UserSub falls back to a single fleet-wide key `user_blocked:unknown` so it still alerts without a user identity.
- Egress hygiene (bridge.go header): only bounded enum fields and the opaque sub reach Summary/Evidence.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/alertpipeline/bridge_test.go (two users on one domain, one user on two domains, email absence).
2. internal/integration/types.go: add Subject.User.
3. internal/alertpipeline/bridge.go: add the user_blocked case in bridgeEvent and the entry in reasonSeverity.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Two blocked users on the same domain produce two Findings; one user on two domains produces one Finding with severity high: `go test ./internal/alertpipeline -run TestBridgeUserBlocked`.
- [ ] The marshalled Finding contains the sub-hash dedup key and Subject.User, and no email string, token or domain: `go test ./internal/alertpipeline -run TestBridgeUserBlockedNoEmail`.
- [ ] An event without UserSub still produces the fleet-wide `user_blocked:unknown` Finding: `go test ./internal/alertpipeline -run TestBridgeUserBlockedNoSub`.
- [ ] Existing bridge tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/alertpipeline`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#212--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT and per request; [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#311--w-p1-vrfy-03) Add identity fields to analytics.Event and the local SQLite store

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-09`](user-block-list.md#912--w-p1-block-09) Add harness scenarios for blocking users and cutting their sessions

### 7/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-07

**Deny console login and sessions for blocked principals**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#242](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/242)

**Context.** A blocked admin must not keep using the console or remove their own block. This ticket checks the block list at the OIDC callback and on every authenticated console request, revokes a principal's sessions when they are blocked, and exempts break-glass so the console stays recoverable. It reads the list from an in-memory snapshot kept in `BlockStore` (W-P1-BLOCK-03), so no request runs a SQLite query. P3 portal tickets reuse this snapshot (W-P3-CSIG-02/04, W-P3-OFFB-06). Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** the store (W-P1-BLOCK-03), the API (W-P1-BLOCK-11) and the offline CLI whose writes refresh the snapshot through the same callback (W-P1-BLOCK-08).

**What to build.** The snapshot, the two checks, session revocation on Add, and direct audit records for the denials.

**Requirements**

- internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go: `BlockStore` keeps an in-memory snapshot (immutable sets swapped atomically) refreshed on every in-process mutation and by the `OnChange` callbacks (W-P1-BLOCK-08's `data_version` watcher invokes them for CLI writes), and exposes `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` (exact sub, lowercase email). A snapshot load failure keeps the previous snapshot and logs; at startup a failed first load fails closed for console login only (login returns 503) and never blocks `/policy`.
- The OIDC callback (W-P1-SSO-03) refuses to create a session when the verified principal's sub or email is blocked: 403 `{"error":"user_blocked"}` and no session cookie. The session middleware (`withSession`, W-P1-SSO-04) rejects requests from a blocked principal with 403 using the snapshot. Break-glass sessions (W-P1-OPS1-08) are exempt.
- `BlockStore.Add` revokes all active sessions of the matching principal through an injected `SessionRevoker` interface (so `BlockStore` does not import the session store): `DeleteBySub` (W-P1-SSO-04) for entries with a sub and a new `SessionStore.DeleteByEmail` for entries with an email. The SSO-04 `sessions` table already stores the login email; the new method compares `lower(email)`. If a future schema lacks the column, this ticket adds it.
- Both denials are recorded directly through the Recorder (they happen before the audit middleware runs): action `auth.blocked_login` (callback) and `auth.blocked_session` (middleware), target `session`, outcome denied, auth_method oidc, actor the blocked principal; the middleware rate-limits repeats per principal to 1 row per minute. No-op when `cfg.AdminAudit` is nil.
- Default behaviour without any block is unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane (blocked_principal_test.go) using the SSO test fixtures.
2. internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go: snapshot, IsBlocked, SessionRevoker hook.
3. SSO callback and session middleware files from W-P1-SSO-03/04 in internal/controlplane: call BlockStore.IsBlocked and return 403; add SessionStore.DeleteByEmail.
4. Record the two audit actions through cfg.AdminAudit.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A blocked principal completing the OIDC callback gets 403 and no session cookie, and one auth.blocked_login row is written: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedPrincipal_LoginDenied`.
- [ ] An admin with an active session is blocked by another admin (Add), their session row is deleted and their next API call gets 403; unblocking does not resurrect the session: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedPrincipal_SessionRevoked`.
- [ ] A session found by email only (entry has no sub) is revoked via DeleteByEmail: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedPrincipal_RevokedByEmail`.
- [ ] Break-glass sign-in still works while every admin is blocked: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedPrincipal_BreakGlassExempt`.
- [ ] No per-request SQLite query is made by the session check (the store is wrapped with a query counter): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedPrincipal_NoQueryPerRequest`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-03`](user-block-list.md#312--w-p1-block-03) Add the CP block-list store and merge it into the served policy; [`W-P1-SSO-03`](console-sso-rbac.md#311--w-p1-sso-03) Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane; [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#411--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF; [`W-P1-AAUD-05`](admin-audit-log.md#58--w-p1-aaud-05) Gate admin audit behind config, check the key id at startup, add segment rotation and a shared CLI recorder opener; [`W-P1-OPS1-08`](ops-hardening.md#811--w-p1-ops1-08) Add POST /auth/breakglass with rate limits, a session, a signed audit row and a Finding

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-CSIG-02`](consent-auth.md#27--w-p3-csig-02) Implement portal login, callback and session store; [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#47--w-p3-csig-04) Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation; [`W-P2-TOKX-02`](token-exchange.md#27--w-p2-tokx-02) Implement token exchange policy checks and JWT minting; [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#17--w-p3-offb-01) Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder; [`W-P3-OFFB-06`](offboarding.md#67--w-p3-offb-06) Audit and test blocked-user refusals across portal and connect

### 8/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-08

**Add offline block add, remove and list commands to the control-plane CLI**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#304](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/304)

**Context.** When the console or the IdP is unavailable, or a script or recipe needs to block a user without a browser session, the operator needs a command line. This ticket adds `warden control-plane block add|remove|list`, which opens cpstate in `--state-dir` directly and uses the same `BlockStore` and validator as the admin API. It follows the offline-CLI rules of the feature set: one admin audit row per write with auth_method `cli`, recorded through the shared opener `adminaudit.OpenForCLI` (W-P1-AAUD-05) so the existing key is used and a new one is never created. A running CP picks CLI writes up within 2 s. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** the store (W-P1-BLOCK-03), the API (W-P1-BLOCK-11), session revocation logic (W-P1-BLOCK-07, which this ticket refreshes via the shared `OnChange`), and approval-gated removal (W-P2-APPR-08).

**What to build.** The three subcommands, an exported `BlockStore` constructor that needs no `Server`, and the `data_version` watcher the running CP uses.

**Requirements**

- `warden control-plane block add [--sub S] [--email E] --reason R`, `block remove --id ID` and `block list [--json]`; each takes a required `--state-dir` and (add/remove) an optional `--admin-audit-key-file` (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`) and works with or without a running CP. `add` prints the new id; exit 1 on validation errors (same messages as the API 400/409/422), exit 2 for an unknown id on remove. `list` opens the DB read-only (`cpstate.OpenReadOnly`).
- Writes go through `controlplane.BlockStore` (W-P1-BLOCK-03) with actor `cli:<os user>`, so validation, email lowercasing, MaxBlockedUsers/MaxBlockedUsersBytes and the unique indexes match the API exactly. The CLI has no console identity, so the self-unblock check does not apply; the docs state that write access to the state dir already allows policy changes.
- Audit: each add and remove appends one admin_audit row through `adminaudit.OpenForCLI` (auth_method cli, action blocked_users.add or blocked_users.remove, target blocked_users, target_ref `block:<id>`); with admin_audit rows present and a missing/mismatching key the CLI exits non-zero and writes NOTHING (the audit append is attempted first or both are in the same unit so a block is never added without its audit row); when the table does not exist the append is skipped with a one-line notice. Reason text never goes to slog.
- A running CP sees CLI writes within 2 s: `BlockStore` gains `Watch(ctx, interval)` which polls `PRAGMA data_version` every 2 s (started by `controlplane.Run` when the store exists) and, on a change, calls `policyServer.Refresh` and the `OnChange` callbacks (so the W-P1-BLOCK-07 session snapshot is refreshed). Workers then receive the new list within 2 s plus one long-poll cycle. A watcher error is logged and the previous state kept.
- cmd/proxy/controlplane_block.go stays thin (rule C1); the logic lives in internal/controlplane (`RunBlockCommand`-style functions). Document the commands in docs/control-plane.md.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in cmd/proxy/controlplane_block_test.go against a state dir shared with an in-process CP.
2. New cmd/proxy/controlplane_block.go: newControlPlaneBlockCmd with add, remove and list, registered under newControlPlaneCmd in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
3. internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go: export the Server-less constructor path (OpenBlockStore) and add Watch; internal/controlplane/run.go: start the watcher.
4. Append audit rows via adminaudit.OpenForCLI; docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a CP running on --state-dir D and a worker long-poll waiting, `warden control-plane block add --email alice@corp.com --reason test --state-dir D` exits 0 and the long-poll returns blockedUsers with alice within 3s: `go test -race ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBlockCmd`.
- [ ] `block remove --id <id>` restores the previous /policy ETag, and an unknown id exits 2: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBlockRemove`.
- [ ] Adding a duplicate email in different case exits 1 with the API 409 message, and add with neither --sub nor --email exits 1 with no row written: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBlockValidation`.
- [ ] After interleaved CLI and API adds and removes, adminaudit.Verify returns ok and each CLI action has exactly one row with auth_method cli; with admin_audit rows present and the key file missing, the CLI exits non-zero and writes nothing (no block row either): `go test ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestControlPlaneBlockAudit|TestControlPlaneBlockKeyMissing'`.
- [ ] A CLI write refreshes the in-memory login snapshot of a running CP within 3s (BlockStore.IsBlocked true for the new entry): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockStoreWatchRefreshesSnapshot`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-03`](user-block-list.md#312--w-p1-block-03) Add the CP block-list store and merge it into the served policy; [`W-P1-AAUD-05`](admin-audit-log.md#58--w-p1-aaud-05) Gate admin audit behind config, check the key id at startup, add segment rotation and a shared CLI recorder opener

### 10/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-10

**Advertise and record worker caps (blocklist/v1) in the heartbeat**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** An old worker decodes the new policy wire without error (encoding/json drops unknown fields) and would look current while silently ignoring the block list. So workers advertise capabilities on every heartbeat and the CP records them, letting the console warn about connected workers that do not enforce the list. This generic `caps` channel is also what later features reuse (group policy W-P1-GPOL-07, hooks, bundles, usercost). This ticket was taken out of W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) and W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) in the 2026-10-19 split pass and replaces the former stub for this key. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** the warning banner and panel (W-P1-BLOCK-04) and any decision the CP makes from caps (P2 and later tickets read them through `WorkersWithoutCap`).

**What to build.** The worker heartbeat body becomes a struct with `caps`; the CP decodes, bounds and stores them per worker and exposes them on the fleet view.

**Requirements**

- internal/config/remote.go (existing): `Heartbeat` currently marshals `map[string]string{"policyETag": etag}`; replace it with a struct `heartbeatBody{PolicyETag string `json:"policyETag"`; Caps []string `json:"caps,omitempty"`}`. New consts `config.CapBlocklistV1 = "blocklist/v1"` and `config.WorkerCaps() []string` returning the sorted capabilities this binary implements (initially only `blocklist/v1`; later features append their own). `RemoteProvider` sends them via a `caps` field set at construction/`SetCaps` by internal/worker (no change to the `ControlPlaneClient.Heartbeat(ctx) error` interface).
- internal/controlplane/controlplane.go `handleHeartbeat` (the body is already capped at 4096 bytes): decode optional `caps`; drop entries that do not match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,31}$`, keep at most 16, de-duplicate and sort. Unknown JSON fields stay ignored, so old and new workers both work.
- internal/controlplane/registry.go: `SeenHeartbeat(proxyID, policyETag string, caps []string)` stores the caps of the LATEST heartbeat (replace, not merge; a worker that stops advertising a cap loses it); `WorkersWithoutCap(cap string) []string` returns the proxy ids of connected (online) workers that lack it, sorted and capped at 100.
- internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: `WorkerView` gains `Caps []string` json `caps,omitempty`, filled in the `SetWorkers` closure (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go:424).
- Only the advertised-cap list is trusted for display; the CP never executes anything based on a cap in P1. The heartbeat still carries no secret, token or request data.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/config (heartbeat body), internal/controlplane (decode, bounds, registry, view).
2. internal/config/remote.go: heartbeatBody, CapBlocklistV1, WorkerCaps, SetCaps; internal/worker wiring passes config.WorkerCaps() when it builds the RemoteProvider.
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go and registry.go: decode and store caps, add WorkersWithoutCap; internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: WorkerView.Caps and the closure.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A worker heartbeat body contains `caps:["blocklist/v1"]` next to policyETag: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHeartbeatCaps`.
- [ ] A heartbeat with caps ["blocklist/v1"] is stored and shown on WorkerView; a heartbeat without caps (old worker) is accepted with 204 and the worker is listed by `WorkersWithoutCap("blocklist/v1")`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestHeartbeatCaps`.
- [ ] Invalid cap strings, more than 16 caps and duplicates are dropped or truncated, and a later heartbeat without a cap removes it: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestHeartbeatCapsBounded|TestHeartbeatCapsReplace'`.
- [ ] WorkerView JSON includes `caps` only when non-empty: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestWorkerViewCaps`; `go test -race ./internal/config ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard ./internal/worker` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#212--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT and per request

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-04`](user-block-list.md#412--w-p1-block-04) Add the Blocked users console panel and worker enforcement indicator; [`W-P2-AREG-03`](agent-registry.md#37--w-p2-areg-03) Add the Agents tab to the CP console; [`W-P2-AREG-05`](agent-registry.md#57--w-p2-areg-05) Bind workers to an agent id and enforce agent_disabled; [`W-P2-SBND-05`](signed-bundles.md#57--w-p2-sbnd-05) Report bundle state through metrics, heartbeat and the fleet view; [`W-P3-PORT-05`](consent-portal.md#57--w-p3-port-05) Bump grant epochs on revoke and report workers without usersecrets/v1; [`W-P4-DGR-04`](delegation-grants.md#412--w-p4-dgr-04) Add the grant subject resolver, delegation mode and rollout guard to the token service; [`W-P1-GPOL-07`](identity-policy.md#1014--w-p1-gpol-07) Report groupPolicy support in the heartbeat and flag old workers; [`W-P2-WBND-07`](identity-enforcement.md#710--w-p2-wbnd-07) Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability; [`W-P3-PUL-08`](per-user-limits.md#810--w-p3-pul-08) Publish fleet cost blocks as costBlockedUsers from the control plane; [`W-P4-PARK-02`](park-notify.md#28--w-p4-park-02) Notify the user once per pending when the agent can park; [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

### 11/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-11

**Add the block-list admin API with audit and self-unblock protection**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** Admins manage the block list from the console. This ticket adds the admin-only endpoints to list, add and remove entries on top of `BlockStore` (W-P1-BLOCK-03), with role checks, admin audit rows and protection against an admin removing their own block. It was split from the original W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49); the console panel is W-P1-BLOCK-04. Dashboard writes are guarded: until SSO sessions replace it, every state-changing call needs the CP dashboard-write bearer and fails closed without one. Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** the store and merge (W-P1-BLOCK-03), the panel (W-P1-BLOCK-04), login denial (W-P1-BLOCK-07) and approval holds on removals (W-P2-APPR-08).

**What to build.** Three handlers behind a dashboard seam, authz entries, a `blocked_users` state hasher and the self-unblock check.

**Requirements**

- Admin-only routes under `/dashboard/api/blocked-users` (ADR 0004 prefix): `GET` returns 200 `{"entries":[{id,sub,email,reason,createdBy,createdAt}]}` (an envelope so W-P1-BLOCK-04 can add `workersWithoutEnforcement` without breaking clients); `POST {sub?,email?,reason}` returns 201 `{id,...,hint?}` (a `hint` recommends keeping both sub and email when only the email is given), 400 on validation failure, 409 on duplicate, 422 above MaxBlockedUsers or MaxBlockedUsersBytes; `DELETE /dashboard/api/blocked-users/{id}` returns 204 or 404. Editors and viewers get 403 from the authz table. Bodies are capped with `http.MaxBytesReader` (8 KiB) and unknown fields are rejected.
- Self-unblock is refused: DELETE of an entry whose sub or (case-insensitive) email matches the caller's own Principal returns 403 `{"error":"self_unblock_forbidden"}` (another admin or break-glass must do it). A caller with no console identity (the CP admin bearer in `console.auth: none`) has no self to protect, so the check does not apply there.
- New dashboard seam `(*dashboard.Server).SetBlockListStore(BlockListStore)` in internal/dashboard/dashboard_blockedusers.go (interface List/Add/Remove plus the caller identity; the dashboard imports neither cpstate nor controlplane). With the seam nil (workers) the routes return 404. A CP without `--state-dir` sets a stub whose methods return 503 `{"error":"state_dir_required"}` and `/policy` is unchanged. Register the routes next to the existing ones in `dashboard.Server.Handler()` (no routes.go yet; rule X9 baseline) and in `dashboard.Routes()`.
- Authz table (SSO-05): GET admin; POST and DELETE admin with `Audited:true`, Action `blocked_users.add` / `blocked_users.remove`, Target `blocked_users`. The route-coverage test must pass. A viewer or editor attempt is recorded as outcome=denied by the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware.
- Audit: register a `blocked_users` StateHasher (W-P1-AAUD-02 `RegisterStateHasher`) hashing the canonical list of sub/email pairs (HMAC; reasons are not hashed), and call `adminaudit.Annotate(ctx, "block:<id>", {has_sub, has_email})`. Every POST and DELETE, including 403s, produces an audit row when audit is enabled. Reason text is never written to slog, metrics, audit details or hash input.
- `created_by` comes from the SSO Principal (`oidc:<sub>`, `breakglass:<user>`) or `cp-admin-token` for the bearer; the handlers pass it to `BlockStore.Add`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane (blockedusers_api_test.go) and internal/dashboard (handler tests with a fake BlockListStore). HTTP tests for dashboard writes authenticate like production: in `console.auth: none` with the CP dashboard-write bearer (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; on main `Config.Token`, after W-P1-WTOK-07 `Config.AdminToken` with fallback to `Config.Token`), and in oidc mode with a session fixture from the SSO tests; a write without credentials is refused by the guard and a test asserts it.
2. New internal/dashboard/dashboard_blockedusers.go: the seam, interface and handlers; register the routes in dashboard.go Handler() and Routes().
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Handler: set the store (or the 503 stub when State is nil), add the authz entries and register the blocked_users hasher.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An admin POST {"email":"alice@corp.com","reason":"offboarded"} returns 201 with a hint, and a worker long-poll waiting on the current ETag returns 200 within 1s with blockedUsers [{"email":"alice@corp.com"}] and no reason field: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_PostWakesLongPoll`.
- [ ] An editor's POST or DELETE gets 403 with an audit row outcome=denied; an admin's succeeds with outcome=ok and before/after state hashes that differ; a request with no session and no bearer is refused and writes no row: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_RBACAndAudit`.
- [ ] POST with neither field returns 400, a duplicate email in different case returns 409, over the limits 422, DELETE of an unknown id 404; an admin deleting their own block gets 403 self_unblock_forbidden and the entry stays: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_APIValidation`.
- [ ] A CP without --state-dir returns 503 state_dir_required on all three routes and serves an unchanged /policy; a worker dashboard returns 404: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestBlockedUsers_NoState|TestBlockedUsers_NotWired'`.
- [ ] The reason text of a request appears in no log line, audit row or hash input (log capture): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBlockedUsers_ReasonNotLogged`.
- [ ] All blocked-users routes have admin-only authz entries: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage`; `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 12/12 · W-P1-BLOCK-12

**Add harness scenarios proving a block survives rollback, restart and CP outage**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The block list is the incident kill switch, so the done-when sentence also requires that a block survives anything that could silently undo it: a policy rollback, a worker restart and a control-plane outage, and that unblocking restores access and returns the served ETag to its previous value. These scenarios need policy versioning (a rollback) and a CP stop/start, which is why they were separated from the enforcement scenarios (W-P1-BLOCK-09, 2026-10-19 split pass). Siblings in the User block list feature (epic #46): W-P1-BLOCK-01 (#47) wire type and validator, W-P1-BLOCK-02 (#48) worker enforcement, W-P1-BLOCK-10 worker caps in the heartbeat, W-P1-BLOCK-03 (#49) CP store and policy merge, W-P1-BLOCK-11 admin API, W-P1-BLOCK-04 (#239) console panel, W-P1-BLOCK-05 (#240) close open sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-06 (#241) Finding per user, W-P1-BLOCK-07 (#242) console login denial, W-P1-BLOCK-08 (#304) offline CLI, W-P1-BLOCK-09 and W-P1-BLOCK-12 harness scenarios.

**Out of scope here:** enforcement scenarios (W-P1-BLOCK-09) and versioned-store internals (W-P1-PVER-01..03, which test rollback themselves).

**What to build.** A `harness` option for a versioned CP and four scenarios.

**Requirements**

- test/harness gets an option that boots the in-process CP with `--state-dir` and `PolicyStore: versioned` (`controlplane.Params.PolicyStore`, W-P1-PVER-01) so the initial import (W-P1-PVER-07) runs; no Docker. Scenario names start with `block_list_survives_`.
- Rollback: alice is blocked, two policy edits are made through the dashboard API, then `POST /dashboard/api/policy/versions/1/rollback` (W-P1-PVER-03) runs; alice stays blocked on every worker and bob is unaffected.
- Worker restart: restarting a worker (harness restart helper) keeps alice blocked once the worker pulled policy again; before its first pull the worker is fail-closed (existing behaviour). CP outage: with the CP stopped and started again (existing `CPClient.Stop/Start`, test/harness/faults.go), alice stays blocked throughout and a block added while the CP was down by the offline CLI appears after the CP returns.
- Unblocking restores her access and returns the served ETag to its value before the block.
- Every scenario ends with `h.AssertCanaryNeverLeaked()`; waits use `h.Eventually`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the versioned-CP option and a worker-restart helper to test/harness (and a harness_test for them).
2. Add test/scenarios/block_survival.go with the four scenarios and register them in scenarios_list.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] After a policy rollback alice is still denied with user_blocked on both workers: `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/block_list_survives_rollback'`.
- [ ] After a worker restart and after a CP stop/start alice stays blocked; a block added offline while the CP was down is enforced after it returns: `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/block_list_survives_restart|TestScenarios/block_list_survives_cp_outage'`.
- [ ] Unblocking restores access and the served ETag equals the pre-block ETag: `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run TestScenarios/block_list_unblock_restores`.
- [ ] `go test -race ./test/harness ./test/scenarios` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.
